tells: 1. The laugh barely builds: across 1 s only the white-sweater woman lifts a hand and the magenta-jacket man turns his head; the purple-top and grey-blouse women at the right table keep the same hands-on-table pose in all six frames, so nothing reads as caused by a line (club-5-strip.png, centre-right table, all frames)

2. The wide reads as a lineup: the front row sits square to camera, upright, with both hands on the table at the same height, all eyes the same way, like a posed group photo rather than people at cabaret tables (club-1-wide.png, front row centre)

3. The back rows are flat dark silhouettes standing at equal spacing, with no seated poses and no motion, and they read as cutouts against the bar glow (club-1-wide.png and club-2-mid.png, upper middle band)

4. Low-poly shoulders and a smeared hand in the face close: the jacket and collar are faceted, and the hand in the foreground is a soft blob; the background man stares blankly at camera with a dead face (club-4-face.png, lower centre hand and right-middle man)

5. Helmet hair and a stiff twisted arm: the curly-haired man's hair is a solid shell, and the green-hoodie man at the right edge has a rigid, oversized arm rotated around the shoulder (club-6-held.png, centre-left head and right edge)

1. The front row sits identically: upright backs, hands on knees, knees together, shins straight down, as if perched on the seat edge; the bodies seem to float in front of the seats instead of sinking into them (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-6-held.png, front row)
2. The second row reads as standing: full torsos clear the seat backs with no seat visible around them, so the raked seating doesn't sell (theatre-1-wide.png, second row centre)

3. The face close breaks: the hood and collar are faceted low-poly, and the people behind her have stretched, blurred textures with untextured red box seats; the mouth is open but the eyes and brows don't take part in the laugh (theatre-4-face.png, whole background and the jacket collar)

4. Reaction spread is thin: a few mouths open at t=12.6–12.8 (mint-top and blonde-bun women), but the front row's hands and torsos don't move and the back rows stay still; the laugh has no body (no shoulders up, no lean back) (theatre-5-strip.png, front row, frames 4–6)

5. The upper house is a field of identical dark heads on a hazy wall, cardboard-flat with no movement, and the man at far right of the front row goes to black (theatre-2-mid.png top half; theatre-6-held.png right edge)
1. The wide and the held frame are almost pixel-identical: no head, hand or posture has moved, which reads as a frozen room on the wide shot (openmic-1-wide.png vs openmic-6-held.png, whole frame)

2. One shared resting pose: almost the whole front row hunches forward with hands clasped between or on the knees at the same angle, so the variety is in clothes, not in bodies (openmic-1-wide.png, front row)

3. Hair and hand artefacts in the close: the yellow-shirt man's hair edge shows dithered strand cards with a hard cutout, the blonde woman's hand behind him is a ghosted, smeared set of fingers, and a blue sparkle hangs in the dark (openmic-4-face.png, right of his head, lower right hand, left middle)

4. The laugh is good but local: the mint-top and brown-hair women lean in and laugh by t=12.6, while the denim and yellow-shirt men stay neutral; reads as a two-person aside more than a room reacting (openmic-5-strip.png, centre right vs left, frames 4–6)

5. Stiff limbs and odd legs: the brown-hair woman's shins turn pink like bare skin under shorts against the dark seat, and the red-jacket man at the right has a rigid, straight-arm pose (openmic-3-mid.png, centre-right legs and right edge)
